dervis-irab:1-4.t:
* I'rab:
(يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ) يسبّح is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); لله is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يسبّح, or the lām is redundant (zāʾida) with the object, and this has been discussed before. ما is the fāʿil (agent), and في السموات is attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما; وما في الأرض is conjoined to ما في السموات.
(لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) له is a fronted khabar (predicate) and الملك a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); وله الحمد is conjoined to له الملك. هو is a mubtadaʾ, على كل شيء is attached to قدير, and قدير is the khabar of هو.
(هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ فَمِنْكُمْ كافِرٌ وَمِنْكُمْ مُؤْمِنٌ) هو is a mubtadaʾ and الذي its khabar, and the clause خلقكم is the ṣila. The fāʾ is a conjunction; منكم is a fronted khabar and كافر a postponed mubtadaʾ; ومنكم مؤمن is conjoined to فمنكم كافر.
(وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; الله is a mubtadaʾ, بما is attached to بصير, the clause تعملون is the ṣila, and بصير is the khabar of الله.
(خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ) خلق is a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), referring back to Allah; السموات is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and الأرض is conjoined to السموات. بالحق is a ḥāl, i.e. "joined with the truth", so the bāʾ is for accompaniment (al-mulābasa).
(وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ وَإِلَيْهِ الْمَصِيرُ) The wāw is a conjunction; صوّركم is a past verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi. فأحسن is conjoined to وصوّركم, and صوركم is the mafʿūl bihi. إليه is a fronted khabar and المصير a postponed mubtadaʾ.
(يَعْلَمُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَيَعْلَمُ ما تُسِرُّونَ وَما تُعْلِنُونَ) يعلم is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "He", referring back to Allah the Exalted; ما is the mafʿūl bihi, and في السموات is attached to an omitted ṣila of ما; وما في الأرض is conjoined; and ويعلم ما تسرّون وما تعلنون is also conjoined.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «له الملك وله الحمد» there is fronting (taqdīm): the khabar is fronted in both to indicate that the two matters are exclusive to Him, the Exalted.
2- In the preceding verses there is antithesis (ṭibāq) between السموات and الأرض, between كافر and مؤمن, and between تسرّون and تعلنون.
3- Al-Zamakhsharī has a question and answer that are exceedingly delightful, which we quote below: «If you ask: how did He make their forms beautiful? I answer: He made them the most beautiful and splendid of all animals, the proof being that a human being does not wish that his form were other than it is, whatever other forms he sees. Part of the beauty of his form is that he was created upright, not stooping, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: "in the best of stature". If you ask: how many an ugly person is there, of disfigured form and repulsive build, whom eyes despise? I answer: there is no repulsiveness there; rather beauty, like other qualities, comes in levels and ranks. Because some forms fall clearly below the ranks of those above them, and when compared with what surpasses them, they are not found pleasing; otherwise they are within the domain of beauty and do not go outside its bounds. Do you not see that you may admire a form and find it pleasing, then see one more pleasing and higher in the ranks of beauty than it, so that your eye shrinks from the first and you find it burdensome to look at it, after having been infatuated with it and having doted on it? The sages said: two things have no limit: beauty and eloquence».

dervis-irab:5-10.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَبالَ أَمْرِهِمْ) الوبال originally means heaviness; from it comes الوبيل for food that lies heavy on the stomach, and الوابل for heavy rain; then it was borrowed for punishment, because it is like a heavy, tangible thing. In the lexicons: الوبال is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of وبل. One says وَبُلَ, of the pattern ẓarufa, yawbulu, wablan, wabālan, wubūlan and wabālatan: [of] a place, it was unwholesome; [of] a thing, it became severe. And وَبَلَ, of the pattern ḍaraba, yabilu, wablan: [وبل] فلانا بالعصا, he beat him with the stick with successive blows; [وبل] الصيد, he chased the game hard. وبلت السماء: the sky poured down heavy rain (al-wabl). استوبل istībālan [of] a place: he found it unwholesome; استوبلت الإبل: the camels feigned sickness from the unwholesomeness of their pasture.
(زَعَمَ) al-zaʿm is claiming knowledge, and it takes two objects. From it is his saying, upon him be blessing and peace: «"They claimed" (زعموا) is the mount of lying». From Shurayḥ: everything has a kunya, and the kunya of lying is "they claimed". Most often زعم falls upon أنْ with the nūn lightened or أنّ with it doubled, with fatḥa on the hamza in both.
(التَّغابُنِ) tafāʿul from al-ghabn, and it is not between two parties but from one, like تواضع and تحامل. Al-ghabn is taking something for less than its value, or selling it likewise. It has also been said that al-ghabn is concealment; from it comes ghabn in selling, because it is concealed. One says غبن الثوب and خبنته when you take up what of it is longer than your measure; so its meaning is diminution. More discussion of التغابن will come in the section on rhetoric.
Moreover, the ghayn together with the bāʾ, as the first and second radicals of a word, has a particular signification of concealment, absence and hiding. One says لحم غاب, i.e. meat kept overnight, and there is the sense of concealment in it. The thicket (al-ghāba) is so called because it conceals whoever is within it, being crowded with trees. زرته غبًّا: I visited him now and then, and the sense of absence from his companion in it is not hidden. Ḥumayd ibn Thawb [Translator's note: so in the source; the poet is usually named Ḥumayd ibn Thawr] said:
زور مغب ومأمول أخو ثقة ... وسائر من ثناء الصدق مشهور
(A visitor who comes at intervals, a trustworthy brother in whom one places hope, and one widely known for truthful praise.)
And you say: love increases with visiting at intervals (al-ighbāb) and decreases with constant attendance (al-ikbāb). ماء غِبّ and مياه أغباب, i.e. distant water that is reached only after an interval. المغبّة is the outcome of a thing, and it is hidden, known only by conjecture. الغابر is the past, and there is no doubt about its being absent; it also comes with the meaning of "remaining", so it is one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād). اغبرّ, with doubled rāʾ, means it became dusty, and [of] the day, its dust grew intense. Those who recite poetry with melodies, are moved to ecstasy, dance and make a commotion are called al-mughabbira, and their ecstatic singing is called al-taghbīr; it is their habit to keep out of sight and hidden. From al-Shāfiʿī: I think the heretics (al-zanādiqa) devised this taghbīr to turn people away from the remembrance of Allah and from reciting the Qur'an. جاء على ظهر الغبراء والغبيراء, i.e. on the back of the earth, meaning on foot. «The green [sky] has not shaded, nor has the dusty [earth] borne, anyone more truthful in speech than Abū Dharr». The needy are called بنو الغبراء; Ṭarafa said:
رأيت بني الغبراء لا ينكرونني ... ولا أهل هذاك الطراف الممدّد
(I saw that the sons of the dust do not disown me, nor do the people of that outstretched leather tent.)
وزففن إليّ ذئبة غبساء [Translator's note: so in the source; apparently "they led a dusky she-wolf to me in procession", an idiom cited without explanation]. And you say: لن يبلغ دبيس ما غبا غبيس, "Dubays will not attain [it] as long as Ghubays is hidden"; it [غبيس] is a proper name for the constellation al-Jady, so called because of its being hidden. خرج في الغبش, he went out in the dusk of the end of night, and نحن في أغباش الليل, we are in the remnants of the night. فلان يتغبّش الناس, i.e. he wrongs them, and it is obvious that he will not confront them openly with wrongdoing [Translator's note: the source's «وبديه أنه لن يبادهم» is unclear; rendered as best as can be read]. غبط الكبش: he felt the ram's back to know its fatness; and غبطه, of the patterns ḍaraba and ʿalima: he was great in his eyes and he wished for the like of his condition without wanting it to cease from him. الغبيط is the saddle on which the howdah is fastened, so it hides the woman riding in it; Imruʾ al-Qays said:
تقول وقد مال الغبيط بنا معا ... عقرت بعيري يا امرأ القيس فانزل
(She says, while the saddle leaned with both of us together: "You have galled my camel, O Imruʾ al-Qays, so get down.")
غبقه, of the patterns naṣara and ḍaraba: he gave him al-ghabūq to drink, which is wine drunk in the evening, when the night hides them [Translator's note: the source prints «يخيفهم» "frightens them", evidently for «يخفيهم» "hides them"]. غبي يغبى غبًا and غباوة the thing, or [غبي] عنه: he did not perceive it or was ignorant of it; and [غبي] الشيء عليه: it was hidden from him and he did not know it. One says: there is in so-and-so a dullness (غباوة) that provides for him; and most of the rich are dull (أغبياء); and what you did is not hidden from me (لا يغبى عليّ). الغباء is hidden ground. This is one of the wonders of our language, so ponder it.

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ نَبَأُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ فَذاقُوا وَبالَ أَمْرِهِمْ وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ) The hamza is for a disapproving, rebuking interrogative, or an affirming, rebuking one. لم is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and jussive; يأتكم is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and نبأ the fāʿil (agent); الذين is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the clause كفروا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; من قبل is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The fāʾ is a conjunction; ذاقوا is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, the wāw is the fāʿil, and وبال أمرهم is the mafʿūl bihi. The wāw is a conjunction; لهم is a fronted khabar (predicate), عذاب a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and أليم a naʿt (adjective) of عذاب.
(ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُ كانَتْ تَأْتِيهِمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ) ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the two punishments of this world and the Hereafter; بأنه is the khabar. أنّ and its noun, and the clause كانت is its khabar; the noun of كانت is latent (mustatir), referring to the messengers, and the clause تأتيهم is the khabar; رسلهم is the fāʿil of تأتيهم, and بالبيّنات is attached to (mutaʿalliq) تأتيهم [Translator's note: so in the source; the more usual parsing makes the hāʾ of أنه the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) and رسلهم the noun of كانت].
(فَقالُوا أَبَشَرٌ يَهْدُونَنا) The fāʾ is a conjunction; قالوا is a past verb and its fāʿil, conjoined to كانت. The hamza is for a disapproving interrogative; بشر is a mubtadaʾ, its being a subject made permissible by the interrogative entering upon it. They have also permitted it to be nominative as the fāʿil of an implied verb explained by what follows, so the question belongs to the chapter of al-ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), the implied form being "Will a human being guide us?" The clause يهدوننا is in the position of nominative as a khabar on the first view, and has no grammatical position on the second, because it is explicative. The interrogative clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
(فَكَفَرُوا وَتَوَلَّوْا وَاسْتَغْنَى اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ) The fāʾ is a conjunction and conveys causation, not immediate succession, i.e. "so they disbelieved because of this saying". وتولّوا is conjoined to فكفروا; استغنى الله is a verb and its fāʿil. الله is a mubtadaʾ, غني a first khabar and حميد a second khabar.
(زَعَمَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنْ لَنْ يُبْعَثُوا قُلْ بَلى وَرَبِّي لَتُبْعَثُنَّ) زعم is a past verb and الذين its fāʿil; the clause كفروا is the ṣila. أنْ is lightened from the heavy [anna], its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); لن is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity, and the clause is the khabar of أن; أن with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of زعم. قل is an imperative verb; بلى is a particle of answer affirming [what was] negated. The wāw is the wāw of oath and ربي is genitive by the wāw of oath, the two being attached to the omitted verb of swearing. The lām occurs in the response to the oath; تبعثنّ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of like letters; and the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents, is the wāw of the plural, an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil [Translator's note: the source says «وعلامة رفعه حذف النون» "the sign of its nominative is the dropping of the nūn"; what is meant is the nūn, which has been dropped; and since the verb is passive, the wāw is strictly the nāʾib fāʿil].
(ثُمَّ لَتُنَبَّؤُنَّ بِما عَمِلْتُمْ وَذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ) ثم is a conjunction for sequence with an interval; لتنبؤنّ is conjoined to لتبعثنّ; بما is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, and the clause عملتم is the ṣila. ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to what was mentioned of resurrection and reckoning; على الله is attached to يسير, and يسير is the khabar of ذلك.
(فَآمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَالنُّورِ الَّذِي أَنْزَلْنا) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), because it occurs in the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if the matter is so, then believe". آمنوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, and بالله is attached to آمنوا; رسوله is conjoined to الله, and النور is also conjoined; الذي is a naʿt, and the clause أنزلنا is an adjective [i.e. the ṣila], the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. أنزلناه.
(وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ) The wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); الله is a mubtadaʾ, بما is attached to خبير, the clause تعملون is the ṣila, and خبير is the khabar of الله.
(يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُكُمْ لِيَوْمِ الْجَمْعِ ذلِكَ يَوْمُ التَّغابُنِ) يوم is an adverb attached to خبير, or to something omitted indicated by the context of the speech, i.e. "you will differ on the day He gathers you". It has also been said that it is the object of an omitted verb, i.e. "remember". The clause يجمعكم is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it, and ليوم الجمع is attached to يجمعكم; it is so named because on it Allah gathers together the first and the last to carry out the reckoning and the recompense. ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the Day of Gathering, and يوم التغابن is its khabar, i.e. the believers will get the better of the disbelievers by taking their places. More about its meaning will come in the section on rhetoric.
(وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَيَعْمَلْ صالِحاً يُكَفِّرْ عَنْهُ سَيِّئاتِهِ) The wāw is resumptive and the clause is new, set out to explain the mutual loss and gain (al-taghābun) and give its details. من is a jussivizing conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ; يؤمن is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and بالله is attached to يؤمن; يعمل is conjoined to يؤمن, and صالحا is a mafʿūl bihi or a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a righteous deed". يكفّر is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), عنه is attached to يكفّر, and سيئاته is the mafʿūl bihi. The protasis and the apodosis are the khabar of من.
(وَيُدْخِلْهُ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ) ويدخله is conjoined to يكفّر, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; جنات is a second mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); the clause تجري من تحتها الأنهار is a naʿt of جنات. خالدين is a ḥāl, and it is plural because it refers back to the meaning of من, which is plural; فيها is attached to خالدين, and أبدا is an adverb attached to خالدين. ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to what was mentioned of expiation and admission to the gardens; الفوز is the khabar and العظيم a naʿt of الفوز.
(وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ خالِدِينَ فِيها وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ) The wāw is a conjunction; الذين is a mubtadaʾ and the clause كفروا is the ṣila; كذبوا is conjoined to كفروا, and بآياتنا is attached to كذبوا. أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and أصحاب النار the khabar; خالدين is a ḥāl and فيها is attached to خالدين. بئس is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame, المصير is the fāʿil, and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "it", i.e. the Fire.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «ذلك يوم التغابن» there is a representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya). The state of the two parties who were able to choose what leads to happiness in the Hereafter, each party choosing what it desired of what it was capable of in place of what the other chose, was likened to the state of those exchanging goods in trade; and what branches out from that, namely each of them taking the other's place, was likened to al-taghābun, because taghābun is tafāʿul from al-ghabn, which is taking a thing from its owner for less than its value; and that only occurs in a contract of exchange, and there is no exchange in the Hereafter. So applying taghābun to what happens there is only by way of representational metaphor. Al-Zamakhsharī's words are: «al-taghābun is borrowed from people's taghābun in trade, which is that some of them get the better of others, because of the blessed taking the places of the wretched which they [the wretched] would have taken had they been blessed, and the wretched taking the places of the blessed which they [the blessed] would have taken had they been wretched».
2- In the verse there is also the figure of mockery (al-tahakkum), which has been met with before. Here He mocks the wretched, because their taking [those places] is not a gain. In the ḥadīth: «There is no servant who enters the Garden except that he is shown his seat in the Fire had he done evil, so that he may increase in gratitude; and there is no servant who enters the Fire except that he is shown his seat in the Garden had he done good, so that he may increase in regret». And in another ḥadīth: «People go out in the morning in two ways: one who buys his soul and thus frees it, and one who buys his soul and thus destroys it».

dervis-irab:11-18.t:
* I'rab:
(ما أَصابَ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ) A new (mustaʾnaf) statement set out to reply to the disbelievers who said: if the Muslims were in the right, Allah would protect them from calamities in this world. ما is negating and أصاب a past verb; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and مصيبة is genitive (majrūr) in wording and nominative (marfūʿ) in position as the fāʿil (agent); the object of أصاب is omitted, i.e. "anyone". إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and بإذن الله is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أصاب.
(وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ يَهْدِ قَلْبَهُ وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; من is a jussivizing conditional noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); يؤمن is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and بالله is attached to يؤمن. يهد is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and قلبه is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the protasis and the apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of من. الله is a mubtadaʾ, بكل شيء is attached to عليم, and عليم is the khabar of الله.
(وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ فَإِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ فَإِنَّما عَلى رَسُولِنَا الْبَلاغُ الْمُبِينُ) The wāw is a conjunction; أطيعوا is an imperative verb, the wāw is the fāʿil and الله the mafʿūl bihi; وأطيعوا الرسول is conjoined to أطيعوا الله. The fāʾ is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); إن is a jussivizing conditional particle and توليتم is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis; the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then there is no harm to Our Messenger in your turning away". The fāʾ is a particle of causation; إنما is [إنّ] made inoperative by [ما] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); على رسولنا is fronted [Translator's note: i.e. a fronted khabar], البلاغ a postponed mubtadaʾ, and المبين a naʿt (adjective) of البلاغ.
(اللَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ) الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا إله إلا هو is the khabar; the i'rab of the word of testimony has been given in detail earlier. على الله is attached to يتوكل; the fāʾ is a conjunction, the lām is the lām of command, يتوكل is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām, and المؤمنون is the fāʿil.
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّ مِنْ أَزْواجِكُمْ وَأَوْلادِكُمْ عَدُوًّا لَكُمْ فَاحْذَرُوهُمْ) The i'rab of يا أيها الذين آمنوا has been given many times. إنّ is a particle resembling the verb; من أزواجكم is the fronted khabar of إنّ and أولادكم is conjoined to أزواجكم; عدوا is the postponed noun of إنّ and لكم a naʿt of عدوا. The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), i.e. "if you know that, then beware of them". احذروهم is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi.
(وَإِنْ تَعْفُوا وَتَصْفَحُوا وَتَغْفِرُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; إن is a jussivizing conditional particle and تعفوا is the protasis, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; تصفحوا is conjoined to تعفوا, and تغفروا is also conjoined. The fāʾ links the apodosis because it is a nominal clause; إنّ, its noun and its two khabars.
(إِنَّما أَمْوالُكُمْ وَأَوْلادُكُمْ فِتْنَةٌ) [Translator's note: in the source the heading of this verse and of the next segment are run together with the preceding text by a typesetting fault; they are restored here.] إنما is [إنّ] made inoperative by [ما]; أموالكم is a mubtadaʾ, أولادكم is conjoined to أموالكم, and فتنة is the khabar.
(وَاللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ) The wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ; عنده is an adverb attached to an omitted fronted khabar, أجر is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and عظيم a naʿt of أجر; the clause is the khabar of الله.
(فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ وَاسْمَعُوا وَأَطِيعُوا وَأَنْفِقُوا خَيْراً لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, because it discloses an implied condition, i.e. "if you know that He, the Exalted, has made your wealth and your children a trial for you, distracting you from the affairs of the Hereafter, then fear Allah". ما is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows as a maṣdar (verbal noun) made accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "[with] your effort and your ability". اسمعوا, أطيعوا and أنفقوا are imperative verbs conjoined to اتقوا. As for خيرا, there are [several views] about it:
1- The view of Sībawayh, that it is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "and bring good for yourselves", like His saying: «انتهوا خيرا لكم»; al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ confined themselves to this.
2- The view of Abū ʿUbayda, that it is the khabar of an implied يكن, i.e. "the agreement (al-ittifāq) will be good" [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently a misprint for «الإنفاق» "the spending"].
3- The view of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ, that it is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a good spending".
4- The view of the Kufans, that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
5- The view of some, that it is the mafʿūl bihi of His saying أنفقوا, on the assumption of an omitted qualified noun, i.e. "good wealth".
لأنفسكم is attached to خبيرا [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently for «بخيرا», i.e. attached to خيرا].
(وَمَنْ يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ) The wāw is resumptive; من is a jussivizing conditional noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; يوق is the protasis, jussive by the dropping of the weak letter, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Translator's note: the source prints «نائب الفعل», evidently for «نائب الفاعل»] is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he"; شحّ نفسه is a second mafʿūl bihi. The fāʾ links the apodosis, and the clause فأولئك هم المفلحون is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من.
(إِنْ تُقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً يُضاعِفْهُ لَكُمْ) إن is conditional and تقرضوا is the protasis, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and الله its object; قرضا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and حسنا a naʿt. يضاعفه is the apodosis, the hāʾ is its object, and لكم is attached to يضاعفه.
(وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ شَكُورٌ حَلِيمٌ) ويغفر is conjoined to the apodosis, following it in the jussive, and لكم is attached to يغفر. الله is a mubtadaʾ, شكور a first khabar and حليم a second khabar.
(عالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ) عالم الغيب is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, العزيز a second khabar and الحكيم a third khabar.
